# Fixtures

`simple.pdf` is a hand-written one-page PDF generated by this repository setup.
It contains the text `RAIT simple PDF fixture` and no external copyrighted source.

`two-pages.pdf` is a hand-written two-page PDF generated by this repository setup.
Page 1 contains `First page of the RAIT fixture` and page 2 contains
`Second page of the RAIT fixture`. It has no external copyrighted source.

## Generated document fixtures

`sample.docx`, `sample.epub`, `sample.html`, and `sample.pptx` are generated
from `sample.md` by running `tests/fixtures/make-documents.sh` with pandoc
3.9. The markdown source contains only text written for this repository:
headings, a bold paragraph, a bullet list with a nested sub-item, a numbered
list, and a small pipe table. There is no external copyrighted source.

`edge.docx` is generated by `tests/fixtures/make-edge-docx.py`, a stdlib-only
Python script that hand-writes a minimal WordprocessingML package (zipfile
plus written-by-hand XML parts). It exercises document-parsing edge cases
that pandoc alone does not produce from markdown: a title style paragraph, a
localized heading style id, a paragraph split across multiple runs, a table
with vertically merged cells, a horizontally spanned cell, a multi-paragraph
cell, and a nested table, bullet and decimal list numbering with a nested
bullet level, a duplicated mc:AlternateContent textbox (a DrawingML choice
and a VML fallback that both hold the same text, as real Word documents do),
and tracked changes (an inserted run and a deleted run). All of the text
content in this fixture was written for this repository and has no external
copyrighted source.

Both scripts are run from the repository root as
`./tests/fixtures/make-documents.sh` and write their outputs back into
`tests/fixtures/`. `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` and `TZ` are set before invoking
pandoc, and `make-edge-docx.py` writes its zip entries with fixed timestamps
and sorted names, so re-running the scripts produces byte-for-byte
reproducible output aside from pandoc's own non-deterministic internals
(such as generated ids), if any.
